title: Reduced fixed locus of a contracting deformation
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ be a geometric correspondence with fixed scheme $F$ and projections $i_F:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$ as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Let $y_C\in C(k)$ and $y_X\in X(k)$ be reduced closed points, and put $Z=\{y_X\}$. Assume $F=\{y_C\}$ as a reduced subscheme of $C$, $c_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically, and $c_2(y_C)=y_X$. Write $I_Z$ for the ideal sheaf of $Z$ and $J=c_1^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C$ for the ideal of $y_C$. Assume
$$c_2^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C\subseteq J,\qquad (c_2^{\cdot}I_Z)^n\mathcal O_C\subseteq J^{n+1}\quad\text{for some }n\geq1.$$
Use the Rees deformation over $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$ of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry], with special-fibre legs $b_i:N_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)/C}\to N_{Z/X}$. Then $c^{-1}(Z\times Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically, the image of $b_2$ is set-theoretically supported on the zero section $Z$, and $b_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically. The special fibre of $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$ is set-theoretically supported on $y_C$. The canonical closed immersion
$$\widetilde F_{d^{-1}Z}= (y_C)_D\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$$
is an isomorphism on generic fibres and induces an isomorphism on reductions. Thus the lifted fixed scheme is a nilpotent thickening of the constant point deformation.

proof.text: Put $W=c^{-1}(Z\times Z)$. On an affine neighbourhood of $y_C$ its ideal is $J+K$, where $K=c_2^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C$. The stabilizing inclusion $K\subseteq J$ makes this sum equal to $J$, so $W=c_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically; the equality is local on $C$ and both inverse images are empty away from this point. The fixed-square relation gives $c_1i_F=d=c_2i_F$. Since the hypothesis identifies $F$ with the reduced point $y_C$ and $c_2(y_C)=y_X$, $d$ factors through $Z$ and $d^{-1}Z=F$ scheme-theoretically.

Apply [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry] to the two legs over the pair $(X,Z)$. Its support criterion applied to $c_2$ and the displayed power inclusion says that the special leg $b_2$ has image set-theoretically in the zero section. Since $c_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$, the zero-section inverse-image clause for the first leg gives $b_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically. The preceding identification $W=\{y_C\}$ lets these be read as statements about the two legs of the special fibre of the correspondence deformation.

Apply the correspondence clause of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry] to obtain $\widetilde c$ and the natural closed immersion $j:\widetilde F_{d^{-1}Z}\hookrightarrow T:=\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$. Step 1 gives $d^{-1}Z=F=y_C$. Its ideal inside $F$ is zero, so the displayed Rees formula is $\mathcal O_{F_D}[0/t]=\mathcal O_{F_D}$: the source is $(y_C)_D\cong D$. The generic-fibre clause of that node identifies $j_\eta$ with the identity of $F\times_k\eta$, proving that $j$ is an isomorphism on generic fibres.

source.place: Corollary 1.4.5 and Theorem 2.1.3(b) proof after it

proof.text: On $T_s=\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)_s$ the two special legs agree, by the fibre-product definition of the relative fixed scheme. At each point of $T_s$, Step 2 puts its $b_2$-image in the zero section, hence its equal $b_1$-image there as well. The equality $b_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ then forces $|T_s|\subseteq\{y_C\}$. The closed immersion $j$ from Step 3 has this special point in its image, so the special fibre has exactly that support.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), final paragraph of the proof

proof.text: The ring $R=k[t]_{(t)}$ is Noetherian: every nonzero element is $t^a u$ with $u$ a unit, and an element of least such exponent in a nonzero ideal generates that ideal. Thus every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its only primes are $(0)$ and $(t)$, so $D$ is quasi-compact, and its single affine chart makes it locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The Rees node makes $\widetilde C_W$ separated and finite type over $D$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] choose a finite affine cover with rings $B_i$ finitely generated over $R$. Since $\widetilde X_Z/D$ is separated, its relative diagonal is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], so its pullback $T\hookrightarrow\widetilde C_W$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). On that cover [def-weil-closed-immersion] expresses $T$ by the affine rings $B_i/L_i$. The images of the finite algebra generators of $B_i$ generate $B_i/L_i$ over $R$, so the finite-cover criterion of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] makes $T$ finite type over $D$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to conclude that $T$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), final reduction comparison; affine Noetherian and reduction details expanded

proof.text: Every point of $T$ maps to either $\eta$ or $s$, the two points of $D$. Step 3 shows that $j$ covers all points over $\eta$, and Step 4 that it covers all points over $s$. Thus its image is all of $|T|$. Its source $D$ is reduced: $k[t]_{(t)}$ is a subring of the field $k(t)$, so its rings of local sections have no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) to this reduced closed subscheme of $T$, with closed subset $|T|$. It identifies $j$ with the reduced induced closed subscheme on all of $|T|$, namely $T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow T$ of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. In particular $j$ induces an isomorphism on reductions. This uses surjectivity on points directly; it makes no inference from the number of irreducible components.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.3(b), final reduction comparison; affine Noetherian and reduction details expanded

proof.text: By Step 6 the ideal of $j$ is the nilradical $\mathcal N_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Step 5 verifies both hypotheses, quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity, of [lem-sc-reduction-nilradical-nilpotent]. Hence $\mathcal N_T^{m+1}=0$ for some $m\geq0$. Thus the closed immersion $(y_C)_D\hookrightarrow T$ is a nilpotent thickening in the power-of-ideal sense [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], proving the final assertion.

split_report.summary: Split the Rees fixed-scheme argument into seven steps using existing nodes only. Retained the imported statement, including that F is the reduced point. Replaced an invalid irreducible-component argument with surjectivity on both fibres and uniqueness of reduced induced closed subschemes; verified Noetherianity and cited uniform nilradical nilpotence for the final thickening clause. Reconciled the Mathlib search record with the durable executed-query log.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the current main-20261015 lem-trf-local-term-locality proof paragraph (2), specifically the Rees specialization and the assertion after Corollary 1.4.5 that the fixed-scheme deformation is generically an isomorphism and an isomorphism on reductions.

tool_uses.why: Generic Noetherian-scheme nilradical nilpotence turns the reduction comparison into a uniformly nilpotent thickening; the trace-formula unit supplies no separate nilpotence lemma.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q48-1c19633aa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 7 steps in full, every cited statement, and Varshavsky math/0505564 at Lemma 1.4.3(a)-(e), 1.4.4, Cor 1.4.5, Def 2.1.1, Rem 2.1.2 and the full proof of Thm 2.1.3(a),(b). After the leg swap (his c_1 contracts; ours is c_2), the hypotheses are exactly his with Z={y_X}. The added hypothesis that F is the reduced point is supplied by the parent's Step 1, so this is not a weakening. Step 1: the ideal of c^{-1}(ZxZ) is J+K=J, and d factors through Z because F is reduced. Step 2: the Rees node, with f=c_2 for the power-inclusion support criterion and f=c_1 for the zero-section inverse-image clause, both with Z'=W; the legs are identified by uniqueness of lifts. Step 3: the zero ideal gives F_D=D, and the node's generic-fibre clause gives the isomorphism there. Step 4: the special legs agree on Fix(c~)_s, so its support is {y_C}. Step 5: R is a DVR; T is closed in C~_W by base change of the relative diagonal, so it is of finite type and Noetherian. Step 6: j is surjective and its source is reduced, so by uniqueness of the reduced induced structure (clause 3) j is T_red. Step 7: the nilradical is nilpotent. Small cases checked: c_2=0 and c_2=x^2 on A^1 (u(1-tu)=0 with 1-tu a unit) and the point. There are no new nodes and no duplicates (rg search), no cycle, no SGA citation. Accepted tool_use: lem-sc-reduction-nilradical-nilpotent, a generic black box. No fixes.
